Reproducing an airline-network comparison

The paper and the target

Sun, M., Tian, Y., Zhang, Y., Nadeem, M., & Xu, C. (2021). Environmental Impact and External Costs Associated with Hub-and-Spoke Network in Air Transport. Sustainability, 13(2), 465.

Target: Figure 4, “The total environmental impact of two airline networks.” It compares total fuel burn and NOₓ, CO, and HC emissions for a ten-airport Chinese case. Only these four original quantities are plotted; no derived CO₂ series has been added.

This course exercise is separate from the semester project’s US-focused, population-weighted exposure comparison. It does not change those modeling decisions.

Does the quantitative comparison agree?

For each quantity, the independently recomputed arithmetic is reduction (%) = 100 × (city − hub) / city. The inputs are the published aggregates, not independently simulated fuel/emissions. The reference reduction percentages below are those stated in Section 4.3.

$reduction_rows
Agreement requires |recomputed − reported| / |reported| ≤ 0.001, using unrounded calculations.
QuantityReportedRecomputedDifference (pp)Relative error0.1% check

Percentage points are not relative percent error. A small percentage-point gap can still fail this strict relative criterion. Three-significant-figure source totals limit attainable precision; rounding could explain the small reduction discrepancies. The tolerance has not been relaxed and no extra significant digits have been invented.

The source disagrees with itself

$discrepancy_rows
Absolute-total checks that fail, with Table 7 as the named reconstruction source.
Quantity / networkTable 7Other sourceReferenceRelative error
  • HC exponent: Figure 4’s city-to-city annotation says 4.14 × 109; its apparent bar height, Table 7, and Section 4.3 instead support 4.14 × 108. Both printed values are preserved in the input data.
  • HC total: hub HC is 1.49 × 108 in the figure/table but 1.48 × 108 in the prose. The earlier planning response used the prose value; the original-figure audit caught the discrepancy before implementation.
  • Units need investigation: the printed hub NOₓ and fuel totals imply about 40 kg NOₓ per kg fuel, whereas Table 3 gives emission indices in the tens of grams per kg. This is an order-of-magnitude warning, not a license to silently divide the source data by 1000.

The qualitative ordering is reproduced from the reported totals. The original annotations, prose, and Table 7 cannot all be matched at 0.1%. This first pass therefore does not validate the paper’s physical emissions estimates or establish a general environmental advantage for hubs.

How the agent was managed

  1. Paper-result audit: verify citation/license, inspect the actual figure and table, preserve conflicting evidence, and set the numerical contract before coding.
  2. Scientific TDD: observe failing tests, implement the smallest calculations, then rerun the complete suite. Tests cover independent arithmetic fixtures, zero/invalid baselines, mass-unit round trips, and scale/order invariance—not a claim that hubs must always emit less.
  3. Reproduction figure: check actual bar heights and labels, preserve the original variable selection/scale, export deterministically, and inspect the resulting image.

These project-local skills adapt reviewed community workflows from obra/superpowers and K-Dense Scientific Agent Skills. No paid service or generative-image tool was used. Skill sources and concrete use · Red/green execution evidence.

What this first pass establishes—and what comes next

The computation is intentionally small: it reconstructs published aggregates and checks arithmetic. This is useful as a reproducibility audit, but it is too limited to claim an independent reproduction of a network/emissions model.

A stronger second pass would implement a small network and the paper’s phase-by-phase fuel/emissions accounting, with explicit demand, aircraft, and flight-time inputs. The missing original demand matrix, trajectory histories, and licensed BADA performance coefficients must be resolved first. Any reduced or proxy-data version would be labelled an adaptation, not claimed to reproduce Figure 4’s absolute numbers.
